title: React Tooling Core Check
description: Check your understanding of React build tools, Vite, Webpack, Babel, linting, formatting, environment variables, source maps, and build inspection.
author: DailyCoder

questions.prompt: What is a production build mainly responsible for?

options.text: Serving unoptimized source files with extra debugging helpers
Transforming, bundling, and optimizing app code for deployment
Running unit tests in the browser only
Replacing React with HTML strings

questions.explanation: Production builds prepare optimized browser assets, usually with minification, bundling, and environment-specific behavior.

questions.prompt: What happens to JSX before it runs in the browser?

options.text: It is transformed into JavaScript function calls
It is sent to the browser as XML
It is interpreted by CSS
It is stored only in source maps

questions.explanation: Build tooling transforms JSX into JavaScript the browser can execute.

questions.prompt: What does Vite use during development to make startup fast?

options.text: Native ES modules and on-demand transformation
A required full production bundle on every save
Server-side Java only
Manual script tags for each component

questions.explanation: Vite serves source through native ESM in development and transforms modules as needed.

questions.prompt: In Webpack, what is a loader commonly used for?

options.text: Transforming files before they enter the bundle
Opening production pull requests
Formatting commit messages
Rotating API keys

questions.explanation: Loaders teach Webpack how to transform file types such as JSX, CSS, or images.

questions.prompt: Which statement about Babel is correct?

options.text: Babel transforms syntax but is not a type checker
Babel replaces ESLint and Prettier
Babel automatically secures all dependencies
Babel is only used for CSS

questions.explanation: The Babel lesson highlights JSX and syntax transforms while noting it does not type-check code.

questions.prompt: Which tools have different primary responsibilities? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: ESLint finds code-quality and correctness issues
Prettier formats code consistently
Source maps map built code back to source
Environment variables encrypt frontend secrets automatically

questions.explanation: ESLint, Prettier, and source maps serve distinct purposes. Frontend environment variables are not automatic secret storage.

questions.prompt: In Vite, which environment variable is exposed to client code by convention?

options.text: SECRET_KEY
VITE_API_BASE_URL
DATABASE_PASSWORD
PRIVATE_TOKEN

questions.explanation: Vite exposes variables prefixed with VITE_ to client code.

questions.prompt: Source maps can help debug production bundle errors by mapping generated code back to original source.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Source maps are specifically useful for connecting built output and stack traces to original source code.
